items.context: The title says 'allow/deny controls' but the system has two different concepts: (1) acceptance_allow/acceptance_deny glob patterns that control which file paths are expected/forbidden in execution, and (2) a general gating concept of approving/rejecting items to proceed. The existing detail page already has a status dropdown (backlog, researching, ready, failed, completed, archived) but shows acceptance globs as read-only chips.

options.label: Editable acceptance_allow/acceptance_deny globs
options.rationale: Makes the read-only glob chips editable so users can manually set file-path scope patterns. This directly addresses the 'workshop agents forget to set' scenario since acceptance globs are what agents auto-populate. Recommended because it matches the description most closely.

options.label: Approve/reject gating controls (separate from status)
options.rationale: Add explicit approve/reject buttons as a workflow gate before execution, distinct from the status dropdown. More of a workflow feature than a fallback fix.

options.label: Both: editable globs + gating controls
options.rationale: Full solution but larger scope. Could be phased.

items.topic: Interaction pattern for editing glob arrays
items.context: The current UI shows acceptance_allow and acceptance_deny as read-only code chips with a show-more expand. We need to choose how users will add/edit/remove patterns.

options.label: Inline chip input with add button
options.rationale: A text input field below the chips with an 'Add' button. Users type a glob pattern and add it. Each chip has an X to remove. Familiar pattern from tag editors. Recommended for simplicity and discoverability.

options.label: Edit mode toggle
options.rationale: Keep read-only display by default, add an 'Edit' pencil icon that switches to editable mode. Less intrusive but adds a state toggle.

options.label: Modal/dialog editor
options.rationale: Open a modal with a textarea (one pattern per line) plus validation. Better for bulk editing many patterns, but heavier interaction.

items.context: The API validates that globs are relative, non-empty, and syntactically valid. We should validate client-side before sending to avoid round-trip errors.

options.label: Simple regex check + API error passthrough
options.rationale: Check for obvious issues (empty, absolute path, special chars) locally, let API be the authority for edge cases. Low effort, reliable. Recommended.

options.label: Full glob syntax validation library
options.rationale: Use a library like micromatch or picomatch to validate glob syntax fully client-side. More thorough but adds a dependency.

items.freeform: Glob + api to check that it’s a real path within the project

items.context: Need to decide when changes are persisted — immediately on each add/remove, or batched with an explicit save action.

options.label: Auto-save on each change (debounced)
options.rationale: Each add/remove triggers a PATCH immediately (debounced). No save button needed. Feels responsive but could cause many API calls.

options.label: Explicit save button
options.rationale: Accumulate changes locally, show a 'Save' button when dirty. Fewer API calls, clearer user intent, easy to discard. Recommended because it matches the detail page's existing edit patterns.

items.topic: Should locked items (queued/in_progress) allow glob editing?
items.context: The detail page currently locks status changes and action buttons when an item is queued or in_progress. Should acceptance glob editing also be locked in these states?

options.label: Lock glob editing on queued/in_progress items
options.rationale: Consistent with existing locking behavior. Editing globs on a running execution could cause confusion. Recommended.

options.label: Allow editing regardless of status
options.rationale: Maximum flexibility. Users might want to fix globs even during execution for the next run.

items.text: The existing PATCH API endpoint at /api/v1/backlog/{kind}/{name} already supports updating acceptance_allow and acceptance_deny arrays. Server-side validation ensures patterns are relative, non-empty, and syntactically valid. No backend changes are needed.

Note: the `swarm-manager backlog update` CLI command is currently returning HTTP 405 for PATCH requests. This may indicate a routing issue in the running API instance. The workshop can proceed — the CLI issue is orthogonal to the UI feature, but should be investigated separately.
